definitions.explanation: A long, snake-like freshwater fish prized in Japanese cuisine, especially when grilled with a sweet soy-based sauce (kabayaki).

examples.japanese: ⟦{夏|なつ}バテ→夏バテ：15545_natsubate⟧⟦{防止|ぼうし}→防止：14571_boushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{鰻|うなぎ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I eat eel to prevent summer fatigue.

examples.japanese: {鰻|うなぎ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{蒲焼|かばや}き→蒲焼き：29221_kabayaki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{伝統料理|でんとうりょうり}→伝統料理：noentry⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: Grilled eel (kabayaki) is a traditional Japanese dish.

examples.japanese: ⟦{土用|どよう}→土用：27533_doyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{丑|うし}→丑：noentry⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{鰻|うなぎ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦{習慣|しゅうかん}→習慣：01429_shuukan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There's a custom of eating eel on the Day of the Ox during doyo.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Eating {鰻|うなぎ} is especially associated with ⟦{土用|どよう}→土用：27533_doyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{丑|うし}→丑：noentry⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧ (Day of the Ox during the hottest period of summer), believed to provide stamina and prevent heat exhaustion.

COMMON DISHES:
- {鰻|うなぎ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{蒲焼|かばや}き→蒲焼き：29221_kabayaki⟧ (grilled eel with sweet sauce)
- ⟦うな{重|じゅう}→うな重：noentry⟧ (eel over rice in a lacquer box)
- ⟦うな{丼|どん}→うな丼：noentry⟧ (eel rice bowl)
- ⟦{白焼|しらや}き→白焼き：noentry⟧ (plain grilled eel without sauce)
- ⟦ひつまぶし→ひつまぶし：noentry⟧ (Nagoya-style eel rice)

NOTE ON SUSTAINABILITY:
Japanese eel (⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧ウナギ) is classified as endangered. Conservation efforts are ongoing.
